assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: "Null name" row, "Blank name" row (missing name); "Invalid email - no at sign", "Invalid email - missing domain", "Null email" rows

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells (null) when not provided — not 'N/A' or 'none'. These are genuinely optional and absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'dietaryRequirements = null, accessibilityNeeds = null' and code passes null

assertions.text: When testing pricing rules, irrelevant inputs (e.g. dietary requirements don't affect price) use value sets or representative values — not blanks (which mean null). Blanks are reserved for genuinely absent/null inputs.
assertions.evidence: Pricing test fixed values: name="Alice Smith", email="alice@example.com" (representative), null for dietary/accessibility (absent)

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: "Scenario | Name | Email..." and "Scenario | Registration date | Group size..."

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Result?', 'Price?')
Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Name', 'Email', 'Registration date', 'Group size', 'Price?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Columns: Name, Email, Accepted?, Error message?, Registration date, Group size, Price?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Early-bird single attendee', 'Missing name') — not outcomes ('Rejected', '20% off').
assertions.evidence: "Null name", "Group of 5 - group discount applies", "Both apply - early-bird wins" describe input conditions/implications

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Both methods contain only: result assignment, assertEquals/assertTrue calls; no conditionals

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Registration input validation") and @DisplayName("Registration pricing and discounts")

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description("""...Fixed for all rows...""" and @Description("""...Base price...""" both use triple-quoted text blocks
